# git

**Distributed version control — the tool this project is distributed with**

- **Version recorded:** 2.47.3
- **Categories:** `workstation`
- **Upstream:** <https://git-scm.com/>

## What it does

Tracks changes to files over time, with full history available offline and the ability to synchronise with remote copies.

## Why you would want it

Every workflow in this catalog assumes it. Hammunition itself is distributed by git rather than by tarball — that difference is one of the stated reasons the project exists — and several manifests install software directly from a pinned git revision.

## Before it will work

Nothing. It is in the base repositories of every supported target.

## Install and launch

- **Installed with the profile:** [`workstation`](../profiles/workstation.md).
- **Install:** `hammunition install git --dry-run`, read the plan, then run it without `--dry-run`.
- **Launch:** Its package ships its own commands and application-menu entry; a unit that ships none gets a generated terminal entry (**D-050**). `hammunition status` lists what is installed.
- **The install needs the network to:** your distribution's package archive.

## Offline use

*Not yet documented for this application.* Read “Before it will work” above for what it needs; the install-time network line above is the only offline fact generated from the manifest. Internet, a local network and a radio link are three different things, and this page does not claim any of them works until it says so.

## How it installs

- apt: `git`

## Known problems

Configure user.name and user.email before your first commit or git will refuse to make one — the only first-run surprise in an otherwise boring, reliable package.

## Keeping it current

- probe: apt policy
- strategy: apt_upgrade
